item.title: Coincidence? I think not!
item.content:encoded:
Survivors of the SCP-001 event are to keep in touch, because it gets lonely out here. And no, I don't mean keep in touch like "let's add each other on Snapchat and then talk like 2 times a year," I mean like, share cool things that happen and actually have conversations. Just because we're not in the same physical space doesn't mean we can't still "hang out" with each other, and I'll be damned if I let distance be the thing that gives me another excuse to be antisocial.

This line aged better than what should've been literarily possible… I miss the outside world so much please help

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There are some pretty funny parts to this. A major issue I have, though, is that there are so many comedic angles involved. Almost every single line is a separate joke, often with little consistency between one another, each making some attempt to garner entertainment or laughter from the reader. To me, a lot of the joke set-ups fall flat, turning this into a slog to get through. The various zany references to other articles on the site seem completely random. I also don't see the connection between the Wendy's references, the break-ups, and the gross-out moments.

I can see there was a lot of effort put into this, and I would suggest just sticking to one theme instead of attempting so many disparate ones.

Shaggy's Proposal was hilarious, but everything else just felt kind of forgettable. I was actually sort of expecting a major tone shift at the end, like all these weird scenarios were just a reality bender screwing around for his girlfriend. Which was what happened, but I was thinking more seriously. I upvoted anyways; it's serviceable enough.

A disgusting, fleshy hand grabs for your underside.

You shout, and jump up, narrowly missing being groped by a slimy creep.

Haha, I'm uncomfortable.

Edit: Voided my upvote because this could be much better and less assault-y.

item.content:encoded: This starts off very well. The narrative portion at the beginning is nicely done; humorous, unexpected, subverts WDB's techniques very well. Elements of this are well done but I don't think it really works as a whole.
